THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY WAS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 14.5 NMI SOUTHEAST OF VENICE, LA AND CONSISTED OF TWO SEGMENTS. THE FIRST WAS ORIENTED NW-SE AND MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 2.5 NMI IN LENGTH AND UP TO 0.5 NMI IN WIDTH. THE SECOND WAS ORIENTED GENERALLY N-S AND WAS TO THE EAST OF THE FIRST SEGMENT, AND MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 2.4 NMI IN LENGTH AND UP TO 0.2 NMI IN WIDTH. UNCERTAINTIES: THERE WERE OIL FACILITIES NEARBY TO THE NORTH, BUT NONE COULD BE DEFINITIVELY ASSOCIATED WITH EITHER SEGMENT. THE TWO SEGMENTS MAY HAVE HAD SEPARATE ORIGINS, BUT WERE ASSOCIATED WITH EACH OTHER DUE TO THEIR PROXIMITY AND LACK OF CLEAR ORIGINS.

properties.summary: Incident Type: RAILROAD - NRC Report ID: 1049050 - Medium Affected: BALLAST - Suspected Responsible Party: CSX
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1049050
Incident Time: 2013-06-02 15:48:00
Nearest City: Lagrang, KY
Location: LAGRANGE, KY FIRST AVENUE CROSSING @ MAIN STREET
Incident Type: RAILROAD
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: BALLAST
Suspected Responsible Party: CSX
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 38.336211, -85.472046 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** RAIL FAN, REPORTED WITNESSING AN EAST-BOUND TRAIN LEAKING AN UNDETERMINED AMOUNT OF OIL FROM THE LEAD LOCOMOTIVE AT THIS CROSSING. CSX LOUISVILLE CTD WAS NOTIFIED AND ADVISED Q50402 WOULD BE STOPPED AND INSPECTED. DISPATCHER, OLDHAM COUNTY, WAS NOTIFIED AND DISPATCHING FIRE UNITS TO THE AREA TO INVESTIGATE. UPDATE: AT 16:15 HOURS, DISPATCHER, OLDHAM COUNTY, ADVISED POLICE WERE EN ROUTE TO ASSIST FIRE UNITS ON SCENE WHO HAD TEMPORARILY SHUT DOWN AUTO TRAFFIC NEAR THE CROSSING DUE TO THE OIL LEAK. CSX HAZARDOUS MATERIALS MANAGER, WAS NOTIFIED AND ADVISED PETIT ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTORS WOULD BE NOTIFIED AND RESPONDING OUT OF LOUISVILLE FOR ANY NEEDED ENVIRONMENTAL REMEDIATION. UPDATE: AT 1624 HOURS, LAGRANGE FIRE DEPARTMENT, ADVISED THEY WERE ON SCENE AND REPORTED THAT A LIGHT SPRAY OF AN UNDETERMINED AMOUNT OF OIL WAS FOUND BETWEEN THE TRACKS AND MAIN STREET FOR APPROXIMATELY EIGHT HUNDRED FEET. FIRE UNITS WERE USING A "KITTY LITTER QUICK DRY" TO ABSORB THE OIL UNTIL CSX PERSONNEL/ ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTORS MADE IT ON SCENE. LOUISVILLE CHIEF TRAIN DISPATCHER WAS UPDATED AND ADVISED A TRAINMASTER WOULD BE RESPONDING TO THE AREA AS WELL TO ASSIST IN REMEDIATION EFFORTS.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 33.546769, -86.832397 (Approximated from street_address)
Reported Spill Volume: 500 gallon
Report DescriptionON JULY 1ST AT 1115 HOURS, THE CALLER WAS NOTIFIED OF A POSSIBLE DIESEL SPILL CAUSED BY A TRAIN DERAILMENT. THE CAUSE OF THE TRAIN DERAILMENT IS CURRENTLY UNKNOWN PENDING AN INVESTIGATION. THE CALLER DESCRIBED THE TRAIN AS AN INTERNAL SWITCH ENGINE. LATER IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE TRAIN RELEASED DIESEL INTO CONTAINMENT ON THE PROPERTY. THE CALLER ESTIMATES IT TO BE AROUND 500 GALLONS DIESEL RELEASED. THERE WAS 1 REPORTED EMPLOYEE FATALITY DISCOVERED PINCHED BETWEEN THE TRAIN IN QUESTION AND ANOTHER RAILCAR. THE CALLER STATED THAT THE IN PLANT TRACKS ARE CLOSED IN ALL DIRECTIONS UNTIL OSHA CLEARS THE SCENE. THERE WERE NO ROADWAYS CLOSED AS A RESULT OF THIS INCIDENT. THE CALLER STATED ALL THEY SAW WAS ONE ENGINE THAT DERAILED. THERE WERE RAILS CARS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS TRAIN, HOWEVER THE CALLER WAS UNAWARE IF ANY DERAILED. THIS INCIDENT OCCURRED AT A MANUFACTURING FACILITY AND THERE IS NO MILE POST OR SUBDIVISION THAT COULD BE PROVIDED BY THE CALLER.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.264494, -83.099586 (Approximated from premise)
Reported Spill Volume: 200 gallon
Report DescriptionEST. 200 GAL (~908 L) OF VEGETABLE OIL SPILLED FROM OPEN PIPE IN THE REFINERY WITH APPROX. 5 GAL (~ 23 L) IMPACTING THE DETROIT RIVER. LOCATION IN WATER IMPACTED IS NORTH OF THE SHIP DOCK, INSIDE THE BAY ON THE NE CORNER PRIOR TO THE LAND JUTTING WEST INTO D. RIVER. WEST OF THE ON-LAND TANK FARM. -CAUSE WAS WORKERS DOING WORK ON THE PIPE, VALVE WAS LEFT OPEN. PUMP KICKED ON AND CREW DIDN"T NOTICE VALVE WAS LEFT OPEN. PIPE HAS SINCE BEEN ISOLATED. NO FURTHER SPILLAGE OCCURRING. -GFL IS ALSO ON THIS CALL AND CONFIRMS THAT APPROX. 5 GAL IMPACTED THE RIVER AND INFORMS THAT ADM A-I CO. CREW DID A GOOD JOB OF CONTAINING SPILL. -2 ROLLS OF ABSORBENT PADS HAVE BEEN DEPLOYED. EACH ROLL IS APPROX. 75" LONG X 3" WIDE. PADS STILL IN PLACE ALONG THE EDGE OF THE SHORE/WATER AND BY THE OUTFALL AREA. SAYS MATERIAL IS TRAPPED IN THE BAY AREA CURRENTLY. NOT REALLY IMPACTING THE MAIN RIVER. -GFL HAS A VACTOR TRUCK ATTENDING (ETA 30 MIN.) TO BEGIN CLEAN UP BY FLUSHING AND VACUUMING UP THE SITE. WASTE COLLECTED WILL BE PROCESSED ONSITE AT THEIR WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY AND RE-INCORPORATED INTO THEIR PROCESSES. -DURATION OF CLEAN UP ESTIMATED AT 4 HRS. -FACILITY CRUSHES SOYBEAN AND CANOLA BEANS FOR OIL. -SAC ADVISED ADM A-I CO. & GFL TO ENSURE SAC IS UPDATED IF THE SITUATION DETERIORATES AND/OR WHEN THE CLEAN UP IS COMPLETED.

Report DescriptionPER REPORT: WE CURRENTLY HAVE A LEAK IN OUR STARBOARD AZIPULL DRIVE. THIS HAS BEEN REPORTED TO CLASS AND WE HAVE A CONDITION OF CLASS ISSUED. WE ARE SCHEDULED TO GO TO DRY DOCK AFTER HALIFAX FOR FURTHER INSPECTIONS / REPAIRS. THE CREW ONBOARD HAVE EXHAUSTED ALL EFFORTS TO INVESTIGATE THE ISSUE INCLUDING DIVERS IN OUR PREVIOUS PORT, PORT FURCHON USA. THE ENGINEERS ARE KEEPING A CLOSE EYE ON THE SITUATION AND ARE CURRENTLY REPORTING NO LOSS DESPITE 0.2BAR PRESSURE ON THE HEADER TANK. WE SUSPECT THIS MAY BE DUE TO THE CHANGE IN WATER TEMPARTURE AS WE PROCEED NORTH FROM THE GULF OF MEXICO / AMERICA. WE HAVE A RELATIVELY HIGH LEVEL OF CONFIDENCE IN BEING ABLE TO KEEP A 0 DISCHARGE RATE HOWEVER WE DO HAVE TO MAINTAIN PRESSURE ON THE OIL TO AVOID WATER INGRESS. GIVEN THIS WE HAVE MADE ARRANGEMENTS TO PROCURE A BOOM THROUGHOUT OUR PORT CALL. WORST CASE LOSS WE HAVE OBSERVED IN THE LAST WEEK HAS BEEN 10L / DAY WITH THE THRUSTER RUNNING OR OPERATING, HOWEVER AS PREVIOUSLY STATED WE HAVE OBSERVED ZERO LOSS IN THE LAST COUPLE OF DAYS.
